transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... my supervisor told me I needed to come. 

I guess... I keep leaving my station on the line. Or, like, popping up during our shift meetings when I'm supposed to just stay put. He said it's becoming a safety problem. I just... I kind of take off before I even really think about it. 

So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
When did you first notice that you had trouble staying in one place or sitting still? Has this been something you've dealt with your whole life, or is it something newer?

Um... I guess my whole life. It's not new. 

Even back in... like, elementary school, I was always the kid who couldn't stay in my seat. Teachers were always sending notes home. Just for... wandering around the room, mostly. Or blurting things out... talking over the teacher. Stuff like that. 

So, yeah. Always.

Back in school, besides the wandering around and blurting things out, did you also have trouble focusing on your work or keeping your attention on what the teacher was saying? Like, would you lose track of assignments or have a hard time concentrating?

Um... no. Not really. 

I mean... I didn't really have a hard time understanding the work or anything. I just... couldn't stay in the chair to do it. So, no. I don't think I lost track of things. Just... the moving around part.

When you're trying to do something that requires focus—like reading instructions or watching a video—do you find your mind wandering to other things, or do you have trouble keeping your attention on it even when you want to?

I mean... maybe a little. 

Like... when I have to do inventory logs at work. Or read the CNC training pages. I start out really trying to focus on it. But after a few minutes, the words and numbers just kind of... blur together. 

I end up having to keep going back over it, because I realize I didn't actually take any of it in. So... yeah. I guess.

Back in elementary school, when you were having trouble sitting still and blurting things out, did you also have the same problem with focusing on your schoolwork—like needing to reread things or your mind wandering—or was it mainly just the moving around and talking out of turn?
I don't really remember. Um... like I said before, it was mostly just the moving around. I don't think I had to reread things back then. Just... couldn't stay put.

Looking back to when you were in elementary school—besides the moving around and blurting out—did teachers or your parents ever mention that you seemed to have trouble paying attention, or that you were forgetful about things like homework or instructions?
I don't think so. I don't really remember them saying that. Just... that I was disruptive. That's all I remember them talking about.
When you were in elementary school, do you remember if you ever lost things—like your homework, pencils, or papers—or forgot what your parents or teachers asked you to do?
Um... no. Not really. I don't remember losing my stuff back then. Just... what I said before. Getting in trouble for not sitting still. That's it.

You mentioned you still have trouble staying in one place at work now. How often would you say this happens—like, is it something that's been pretty constant since school, or did it get better for a while and then come back?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess it's just... always been like that. It happens a lot at work. I don't think it ever really stopped or anything. Just always been this way.

When you were in elementary school, do you remember having trouble paying attention in class—like your mind wandering during lessons, or having to reread things to understand them—or was it really just the moving around and talking out of turn?
Um... like I said before, no. I don't really remember that. It was really just the moving around. I didn't have trouble with the other stuff... just couldn't stay in my seat.

When did you first start having trouble with your mind wandering and needing to reread things—like with those inventory logs and training pages? Was that something that started recently, or has that been going on for a while?

Um... I don't know when it started exactly. I just know it happens now. Like, I'll be looking at the inventory logs, or trying to get through those CNC training pages... and I start out really trying to focus. But after a few minutes, it's just... the numbers and words kind of blur together. I have to keep going back over it because I realize I didn't actually take any of it in. I guess it's been going on for a bit.

When you think back to elementary school, even though you don't remember teachers complaining about it—do you remember if you personally noticed your mind wandering during class, or if you had to reread things to understand them back then?
I... no. I don't really remember that happening back then. I just couldn't sit still.
